title: Original pad to Bluetooth keyboard, pad-ble v1
intro: Two original NES controllers into an ESP32-C6, which presents them to a phone or a laptop as a plain Bluetooth keyboard. It is the bench bridge's own pad poll with a radio behind it instead of a shift register, and it stands alone: no Pi, no UNO, no console.

THIS IS A DRAWING, NOT A BUILD. Nothing here has been made and nothing about the circuit has been measured. The firmware compiles and its key mapping passes on the desk; no pad has been wired to it and no host has paired it. It rests on one thing open since 2026-09-07: that an original pad's 4021 follows its buttons at 3.3 V. The datasheet says it should; this bench has not seen it.

What HAS been measured is the board rather than the circuit. The part was identified off its own silkscreen, which reads RGB@IO8 and so names a C6 and not an S3, and its header order was read by hand from photographs, sixteen pins a side, because the bench eye cannot resolve a silkscreen that small. Those readings are what let the breadboard sheet say which hole.
revisions: drawn as the buildable subset of the pad adapter: no cell, no charger, no switch
S3 pin numbers removed; GPIO4, GPIO5 and GPIO15 are strapping pins on the C6
one pullup per pad: R1 and R2 had both been drawn on pad 1's data line
devkit headers read off the part, breadboard sheet drawn from them
the second pad removed: a keyboard report has six key slots, and it was never sent
the sheet's own summary stopped saying a second pad is polled; it is not
the devkit's two header rows were drawn swapped; every address moves from row J to row A
